entries.title: Survey on the metric SYZ conjecture and non-archimedean geometry
entries.abstract: We survey the metric aspects of the Strominger-Yau-Zaslow conjecture on the existence of special Lagrangian fibrations on Calabi-Yau manifolds near the large complex structure limit. We will discuss the diverse motivations for the conjectural picture, what the best hopes are, and a number of subtleties. The bulk of the survey highlights the role of pluripotential theory, and non-archimedean geometry in particular, with a list of open questions.

entries.title: Degeneration of Calabi-Yau metrics and canonical basis
entries.abstract: For polarised degenerations of Calabi-Yau manifolds whose essential skeleton has dimension $1\leq m\leq n$, we show that the $C^0$ potential theoretic limit of the Calabi-Yau metrics agrees with the non-archimedean Calabi-Yau metric on the Berkovich analytification. Moreover, this limit data can be encoded into the unique minimiser of the Kontorovich functional of an optimal transport problem, under some algebro-geometric assumptions on the existence of a canonical basis of sections for tensor powers of the polarisation line bundle.

principal_claims.source: Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.2, pages 2–3; proof Section 4, pages 24–33
principal_claims.claim: For a polarized meromorphic degeneration of smooth projective Calabi–Yau manifolds, with a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic volume form and essential dimension 1 through n, normalized metric norm powers 1/abs(log(abs(t))) converge continuously in the hybrid topology to the normalized non-Archimedean Calabi–Yau metric.
principal_claims.book_admission: Pending recorded proof and dependency repairs.

principal_claims.claim: Optimal-transport characterization assumes maximal essential dimension, regular section bases in every tensor degree that remain bases centrally, global valuative independence, indexing by rational points of an integral polyhedral complex, and the stated multiplication law modulo t. The valuation-based cost is not simply assumed to be the bilinear pairing and is initially defined on face interiors.
principal_claims.book_admission: No new theorem import; all extra hypotheses must be retained.

principal_claims.claim: The specific intermediate-complex-structure hypersurface family has a weighted transport analogue with W(p)=(1+sum_i d_i p_i)^(n-m); this is not a statement for every intermediate degeneration.

General theta valuative independence, metric SYZ fibrations, and mirror cost reciprocity remain questions or proposed strategies in this paper. Potential convergence is not a proof of the full metric SYZ conjecture.

findings.source: Section 3.3 definition, page 14; Lemma 3.11 and Remark 3.13, page 15
findings.finding: The printed componentwise strict order excludes equality and the natural sum interpretation of the denominator makes every graded quotient zero in the common-basis case of Remark 3.13 when dimension is at least two. Write m_i=max_k mu_{i,k}; then F_mu=direct_sum_i t^(m_i) R theta_i. Increase all coordinates belonging to index i to obtain mu^(i)>mu. For i!=j, F_mu^(i)+F_mu^(j)=F_mu, since each summand contains all other basis directions. Hence gr_mu=0 for every mu, and the sections lifted from these quotients cannot generate the nonzero vector space as Lemma 3.11 asserts.
findings.scope: Exact internal algebra check of the printed auxiliary construction; not a counterexample to Calabi–Yau hybrid continuity. The external direct-sum symbol in the quotient also needs a defined image; interpreting it as a sum of submodules does not resolve the collapse.
findings.potential_repair: Corollary 3.16 already suggests a finite family of columns of meromorphic inverse constraint matrices. A determinant-minimizing finite-basis argument may bypass Section 3.3; an independently written proof is the next research step.
